Kanimozhi explains DMK's support for Delimitation Bill, says party has not changed standDelimitation Bill Highlights: INDIA bloc leaders on Saturday decided to jointly oppose the Centre's proposed Delimitation Bill and the linked constitutional amendment, following a meeting at the Delhi residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. Addressing a press conference after the meeting, Kharge described the proposed legislation as a "grave threat to democracy" and accused the Modi government of seeking to consolidate power. The Opposition also raised concerns over the proposed 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats, which would take the House's maximum strength to 850. The bloc outlined three key demands: retaining the existing strength of the Lok Sabha, implementing the 33 per cent women's quota within the current number of seats, and keeping the allocation of seats among states unchanged for the next 25 years. The meeting was attended by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, RJD's Manoj Jha and other Opposition leaders. However, differences have emerged within the Opposition, with the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) backing the revised proposal on the condition that all states receive a uniform 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats.
